Methods for Fitted Models

Source: R/methods.R
OneSampleMR-methods.Rd

Extract the estimated parameters, their variance-covariance matrix, Wald confidence intervals, the number of observations, and the model formula from models fitted by msmm(), lsmm(), tsps(), and tsri().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'msmm'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsmm'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tsps'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tsri'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'msmm'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsmm'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tsps'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tsri'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'msmm'
confint(object, parm, level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsmm'
confint(object, parm, level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tsps'
confint(object, parm, level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tsri'
confint(object, parm, level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'msmm'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsmm'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tsps'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tsri'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'msmm'
formula(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsmm'
formula(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tsps'
formula(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tsri'
formula(x, ...)

Arguments

object

a fitted model object of class "msmm", "lsmm", "tsps", or "tsri".

...

further arguments passed to or from other methods.

parm

a specification of which parameters are to be given confidence intervals, either a vector of numbers or a vector of names. If missing, all parameters are considered.

level

the confidence level required.

x

a fitted model object of class "msmm", "lsmm", "tsps", or "tsri".

Value

coef() returns a named vector of the parameter estimates, vcov() their variance-covariance matrix, confint() a matrix of Wald confidence limits, nobs() the number of observations, and formula() the model formula.

Details

The parameters are those of the underlying GMM (or, for the "tsls" and "tslsalt" methods of msmm(), two-stage least squares) fit, on the scale on which they are estimated. For example, the causal effect parameter of msmm() is a log causal risk ratio and that of lsmm() a log causal odds ratio. The exponentiated causal effect estimates are available in the crrci (MSMM), corci (LSMM), and estci (TSPS and TSRI) elements of the fitted objects, and are printed by their print() and summary() methods.

Examples

set.seed(123456)
n    <- 1000
G1   <- rbinom(n, 2, 0.5)
G2   <- rbinom(n, 2, 0.3)
G3   <- rbinom(n, 2, 0.4)
U    <- runif(n)
X    <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(0.7*G1 + G2 - G3 + U))
Y    <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-2 + 0.5*X + U))
dat  <- data.frame(G1, G2, G3, X, Y)
fit  <- msmm(Y ~ X | G1 + G2 + G3, data = dat)
coef(fit)
#>   E[Y(0)]         X 
#> 0.1826755 0.4502279 
vcov(fit)
#>              E[Y(0)]           X
#> E[Y(0)]  0.002703329 -0.02131077
#> X       -0.021310766  0.17479198
confint(fit)
#>               2.5 %   97.5 %
#> E[Y(0)]  0.08077005 0.284581
#> X       -0.36919642 1.269652
nobs(fit)
#> [1] 1000
formula(fit)
#> Y ~ X | G1 + G2 + G3
#> <environment: 0x6186504002b0>
